aim: A fenced reserve holds a small group of deer. A switch turns reproduction on or off, and a clock runs ten years in seconds. Beside it, a board shows a real line graph of children per woman in a small country.

aim: A small model room has a lamp, a socket, a kettle and a wet sink. A second corner has a lamp, a television and a charger, with a meter that counts the electricity used in one day.
bigIdea: Electricity must be handled with care: never with wet hands, and never through damaged wires. A hazard is something that could cause harm. We spot it before anyone is hurt. safety: Electricity and water must never meet. Use dry hands only, and never handle a wire with damaged covering.

aim: A toy lighthouse has a glass tower and a lantern. A tray beside it holds a battery, a bulb, wires and a switch. Build its circuit so the lantern lights.
bigIdea: A working toy circuit follows the same rules as any circuit. A battery, wires and a bulb are joined in one complete loop. Every clip must be fastened. Building a switch into a circuit lets it be turned on and off easily. Understanding circuits lets us design things that use electricity on purpose.
safety: Never join the two ends of a battery with a bare wire.

challenge.q: A pupil says, "The toy will work as long as the battery, wires and bulb are all inside it." Is the pupil right?
challenge.answer: No. The parts must form one complete loop. A gap anywhere stops the light.
mixups: Yes. The parts do not need to be joined together, because they are all inside the toy.
Yes. Only the place of the bulb matters, and the clips can be left open.
Yes. The toy's body completes the circuit, so the clips are not needed.
challenge.why: A circuit works only when the battery, wires and bulb are joined in one unbroken loop. A gap or a loose clip stops the light.

challenge.q: One clip in the toy's loop is left open. What happens to the light?
challenge.answer: It stays off, because the loop has a gap.
mixups: It comes on dimly.
It comes on, because the main parts are inside.
It flickers on and off.
challenge.why: An open clip leaves a gap in the loop. The circuit is open, so electricity cannot flow all the way round.

challenge.q: A toy has no bulb in its holder. Will the light come on?
challenge.answer: No. The loop is open where the bulb belongs.
mixups: Yes. The wires carry the glow all the way round to the lantern.
Yes, but only dimly.
Only if the clips are fastened.
challenge.why: The bulb is part of the loop. Without it the loop is open, so no light comes on.
